question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-\operatorname{arsech}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡x)) \\  & =-(-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\sqrt{1-{ln}^{2}⁡x}})\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡x)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡x\sqrt{1-{ln}^{2}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡x\sqrt{1-{ln}^{2}⁡x}}.\end{aligned}
$$
